First prediction (calls raise it, from about the third call): at the typical customer, the unit is 0.26 at no calls, 0.33 at two, 1.91 at four and 4.46 at seven; through this part the score gains 1.54 at four calls against 0.21 at none. Second prediction (heavy day use closes it): the same customer with 300 day minutes (day charge set to match) has the unit at 0.00 at no calls and still 0.00 at six calls; it opens only at seven (0.36). At the typical number of calls the unit reads day minutes only (not day charge): it is 0.96 at 160 minutes and 0.00 at 200 minutes. Self-probe passed. In the whole model this unit also flattens the day-usage effect for light users: at 100 day minutes the direct plan-and-usage terms give -2.72 while this unit gives 2.44, so a light user's predicted risk (4.5%) is a little above the typical customer's (2.5%).
